title: Red Eye Ruby
description:
Red Eye Ruby is a Minneapolis-based retro roots-rock and neo-soul band blending the soulful grit of Amy Winehouse with the rhythmic pulse of New Orleans. Drawing from jazz, blues, folk, and R&B, their original music pairs vintage glow with modern bite, lush grooves, guitar-driven arrangements, and unflinching lyrics about womanhood, labor, resilience, and life in the male-dominated music industry. 

An established presence in the Twin Cities music scene, Red Eye Ruby has held residencies at Palmer’s Bar, The Hook and Ladder Theater, and the 331 Club. Their music has earned repeated Minnesota Public Radio recognition, with “Sunshine & Good Lookin’” featured by The Current in 2022 and “Burning Sunbeams” selected as an MPR News Song of the Day in 2026. Known for commanding, high-energy performances led by powerhouse vocals and expressive guitar work, Red Eye Ruby delivers a sound that feels both timeless and unmistakably current.

description: Smokin’ Joe (Joe Scarpellino) is a high-energy paradoxical musical dynamo specializing in heartfelt cerebral lyrics and dark-electro funk-rock grooves. Joe is known for deeply connecting with his audience through his catchy and thought-provoking songwriting style. While his honest and passionate songwriting may bring many of his fans to tears, it’s his seductive beats and funkadelic bass lines that get every booty on the dance floor.

title: DGS VLN
description:
Performing on a five stringed instrument, DGS (pronouns: they/them/theirs) has both violin and viola at their fingertips, and the addition of live effects expands their sound palette to become a one-person orchestra. With a tap on the body of the instrument, the violin transforms into a kick drum. A synth pedal shifts the octaves down into bass territory, while pizzicato in their hands is performed like a guitar or mandolin. Ambient reverbs create synth textures uniquely voiced by the instrument’s timbre, and all of these sounds are created and captured live with a looper to create their music while stitching in soaring melodies over top. Their music has been described as "cinematic pop", "if Hans Zimmer wrote for Top 40 radio", and "organized chaos in musical form". 

DGS has a way of speaking through their music that captivates any and all who stop to listen.

title: Ben Cook-Feltz
description: Described by Iowa Public Radio as "Paul Simon singing songs about broken hearts and pants," Ben Cook-Feltz is a singer, songwriter, keyboardist and occasional drummer. Combining observational, subtly quirky lyrics with melodies that hearken back to the classic sounds of the 60′s and 70′s, he has been entertaining and confusing audiences throughout the Midwest (but mostly Minnesota) as a dynamic performer, whether playing solo, with his crackerjack band, or supporting some of the finest regional talent (Mother Banjo, Haley E Rydell, Jaspar Lepak). His most recent record, Cook-Feltz Sings Son of Schmilsson, was released in August 2025 and was hailed as “expertise and precision at its finest; art with a limitless sense of fun” (Adventures in Americana). When not indulging in his rockstar delusions, Cook-Feltz is a devoted father, cycling enthusiast and lifelong Godzilla fan.

title: Artu Duo
description:
Now in their 16th year as Artu Duo, pianist Garret Ross and cellist Ruth Marshall are based in Minneapolis and Saint Paul, MN, and enjoy concertizing and teaching together both on tour and at home. 
After forming in 2011, Artu Duo completed a residency course on the Beethoven Sonatas and Variations for Cello and Piano at the Banff Centre in Canada. In 2012, Artu Duo traveled to the Aldeburgh Festival in England, where they completed a residency course on the chamber music of Brahms and Schumann. These immersive experiences sparked a deep love of the music of Beethoven, Brahms and Schumann in Artu Duo, which has been the foundational repertoire for them ever since- not only as a duo, but as a piano trio, quartet, and quintet, when joined by colleagues. From that foundation, Artu Duo has explored and championed an incredibly broad repertoire, including canonic works, contemporary and rarely-heard works, and particularly music written by women, people of color, and living composers.  
Artu Duo has toured extensively in the United States, playing concerts in Indiana, Illinois, Wisconsin, Iowa, Oregon, Montana, Washington, New York, California, Minnesota, and Louisiana. In both 2013 and 2016, Artu Duo played on the Dame Myra Hess Memorial Concert Series in Chicago, which was broadcast live on WFMT. And in 2016, they gave their debut at Carnegie Hall, playing a complete program in the Weill Recital Hall. They have performed the Beethoven Triple Concerto as soloists with the Winona Symphony Orchestra (2021) and the Wartburg Community Symphony (2022). 
Mr. Ross and Ms. Marshall are both committed teachers, and have enjoyed giving masterclasses and performing outreach concerts while on tour. Artu Duo community and educational performances have been presented by the Illinois Symphony Orchestra, the Saint Paul Conservatory, the Bozeman Symphony Orchestra, the Mineral Point Chamber Music Festival, Minnesota Public Radio, and through the Britt Festival Education and Engagement resident artists program. Additionally, Artu Duo has given collegiate-level masterclasses at the Apollo Music Festival, the University of Louisiana, the State University of New York at New Paltz, Indiana State University, and Humboldt State University. https://www.artuduomusic.com/

description:
A soulful blend of delta blues, cosmic country, and a little bit of house music.
​

Their debut album "The Chariot" was recorded by Holly Hansen at Salon Sonics in Minneapolis and mixed by Nat Harvie and in 2025 Sawtooth Witch's lead single "The Hustle" was considered Best new Music by MSP Magazine, RACKET, and 89.3 The Current

title: Ryan Traster
description: Ryan Traster is a Twin Cities based Americana artist and songwriter. With 20+ film/TV syncs and a career spanning two decades, his new EP Lifers (produced by Kevin Bowe) marks a return to big-hook Heartland rock and gritty, Kristofferson-style storytelling. A veteran collaborator (Chris Walla, The Jayhawks) and a "lifer" in the truest sense, Traster blends a low, twangy vocal with the melodic sensibilities of the great American songbook.

title: Pullstring
description:
Midwest Britpop, Alt-Rock, Pop-Punk in denial… you get the idea. Hailing from Minneapolis, Pullstring’s nostalgic brand of alt-rock channels the energy of the ’90s and early 2000s. Paying homage to influences like Green Day and The Replacements, the band delivers a high-energy live show anywhere there’s a PA and a crowd willing to listen.

Underneath the driving guitars and infectious melodies, Pullstring explores the tension and tenderness of being a young adult in the 2020s. Their lyrics confront loneliness, shifting identity, and the early sparks of relationships with honesty and relatability. Yet even in their most vulnerable moments, the band threads in a sense of humor and lightness that keeps their sound warm and inviting.

With 100+ shows under their belt, Pullstring is no stranger to life on the road. They’ve taken their high-energy set to venues including 7th Street Entry (Minneapolis, MN), the Maintenance Shop (Ames, IA), and Shank Hall (Milwaukee, WI), and have appeared on festival lineups such as Big Turn Music Fest, KURE Fest, Rochester Thaw, and Taste of MN. Along the way, they’ve shared the stage with touring acts like ALEXSUCKS, George Clanton, The Melismatics, and We Are Scientists.

What will Pullstring do next?

title: Dr Artika Tyner
description:
Dr. Artika Tyner is committed to creating a world of inclusive leaders who will meet the pressing needs of today and work towards a better future where racial justice and economic justice reign supreme.  As a motivational speaker, author and educator, Dr. Tyner helps people of all ages connect with their gifts and develop tangible tools for bringing forth sustainable, durable change in the family, workplace, community or school.  By building and leveraging the tools in The Inclusive Leader she has inspired thousands of people to lead with their own gifts and plant a seed of social change.

Dr. Tyner’s work is grounded in extensive experience as a law and leadership professor, lawyer, social change agent, researcher and nonprofit founder and leader.  She is well-known as a thought leader, author and designer of high-profile programs to drive organizational DEI initiatives and create inclusive leaders.  Her impact spans Fortune 500 companies, start up tech companies, healthcare providers, government services and agencies, higher education institutions and grassroots organizations.  

Dr. Tyner is deftly able to ask the big questions, strategically innovate real solutions and then lead the way. She intentionally invests her time and energy in inspiring change and welcomes opportunities to present, collaborate and innovate with key stakeholders seeking to impact social change and do what no one has done before.

title: Debra J. Stone
description: Debra J Stone is a Jerome Hill Arts Fellow in Literature 2023-25, a recipient of several Minnesota State Arts Board grants, and The Loft Mirrors and Windows Fellow 2023 for writing books for BIPOC children and young adults. Her debut novel, The House on Rondo, was a finalist for the Minnesota Book Award in the Middle Grade Fiction category. Her novel was also a finalist in the Children’s category for the Midwest Independent Publishers Association Midwest Book Awards. The House on Rondo is published by the University of Minnesota Press. Debra resides in Minneapolis with her husband and dog Ruby, a rambunctious Red Heeler Australian Cattle Dog. You can find more information about Debra and her writing at debrajeannestone.com and on Instagram @debra2036.

title: Care and Repair: A Reading
description: As Rumi said, “The wound is the place where the light enters you.” Like it or not, pain, wounds, and breaking are a part of life. Wounds are also an unfortunate byproduct of our life on this planet, especially as the scars of human industry become visible everywhere. How do we care for ourselves, our communities, our loved ones, and our planet in the face of all that is broken? How can repair be an act of creation, building something new and more enduring? Readers Terri Matilla, Jennifer Hildebrandt, Suzanne Swanson, Jennifer Filardo and Heather Quinn will explore care and repair across bodies, communities, families, and landscapes, asking what it means to not only survive damage, but to find new hope within all that is broken.

title: Acts of Magic: A Worldbuilding Workshop w/Cody Klippenstein (limited to 12)
description: In this generative workshop, you are both artist and architect, bringing a new world to life from your imagination, imbuing it with a touch of magic, and populating it with unique characters. First, you'll create on a grand scale, inventing your own fantasy settings rich with detail through a series of prompts, creative exercises, and even optional extra twists and challenges designed to ward off writer’s block. Then, you'll create in miniature by placing a character inside your world and discovering what happens when they move through it.

title: Making Home: A Reading
description: The idea for the Midway Music and Arts Fest came from a group of strangers gathering together around two powerful ideas: first, they were neighbors; and second, they believed that neighbors stand up for neighbors. Neighborhoods and communities are not neutral concepts. The complicated dance of immigration, settlement, displacement, and accommodation shapes the home that we make here together. Readings from writers Patti Kameya, Hawona Sullivan Jansen, Carrie Pomeroy, Alison Morse, and Savannah Dotson explore who gets to call a place home, whose stories are told, and how communities respond when their neighbors are threatened.

title: Dance Showcase
description:
A dance showcase featuring performances by St. Paul Ballet Studio Company, CAAM Chinese Dance Theater, and Young Dance Performing Company

Saint Paul Ballet's Studio Company, made up of the school's upper-level dancers, presents a 20-minute showcase of selections from its repertoire. Join us in the Saint Paul Ballet lobby to see the strength, artistry, and confidence of these dancers up close.

CAAM Chinese Dance Theater will present three dances: 

Impermanence 水墨丹青图 (Duet)
 Life is unpredictable, and people come in and out of our lives all the time. This long-sleeved dance reminds us to cherish every day with those we love.

Song of the Sword 剑之歌 (Solo)
The dance fuses the stylistic essence of classical Chinese dance with elements of swordsmanship, employing ever-shifting movements and nuanced emotional layers to portray a character's inner fortitude and spirit.

Lotus Shadows in the Breeze 风荷丽影 (Quartet）
Young dancers portray the tranquility and vitality of a summer lotus pond through soft, refreshing movements, unfolding a scene filled with innocence and natural beauty.

Since 1987, Young Dance has been transforming lives through movement by creating spaces where people discover themselves, connect with others, and express their artistic voices. 
Young Dance Performing Company, led by Artistic Director Anat Shinar, brings together dancers ages 7 to 18 of all abilities to explore their artistry through technique, choreography, improvisation, and creative collaboration. Throughout the year, dancers work with Young Dance faculty and professional guest artists to develop original work, deepen their skills, and engage with an annual artistic theme. The Company performs in a variety of community settings throughout the year, culminating in a season finale that celebrates the dancers’ creativity, growth, and unique voices. 
For the inaugural Midway Music and Arts Festival, Young Dance will share two original works: a new work created collaboratively by the dancers and a recent favorite from their repertoire by Guest Artist Brian J. Evans.
Learn more about Young Dance at www.youngdance.org

description: We are excited to present Hachijo Daiko. This is an interactive performance where we will ask the participants to try Hachijo Daiko. The less experience, the better!

It's a joyful, high-energy celebration of the artistry, romance, and magic that made Hollywood musicals timeless.

title: The Mercy of Events
description:
Jade Hoyer
The Mercy of Events


Inspired by the artist's experience at Lake Michigan during the COVID-19 pandemic, "The Mercy of Events" serves as a large-scale portrait of one of the world's greatest bodies of fresh water. The exhibition features 90,000 watercolor circles meticulously assembled on graph paper using actual lake water for the paint to create a pointillist-style representation. By blending influences from Seurat’s pointillism and childhood standardized tests, the work explores the act of processing events through a playful subversion of visual order.

title: The Vane Visiting Writer: Reading and Writing When the World Seems Lost -- Deb Olin Unferth in conversation with Patrick Cottrell
description: Reading and writing can offer new ways of understanding ourselves and the world around us, particularly in times of personal, cultural, and environmental loss. In this conversation, author Deb Olin Unferth and alumnus and novelist Patrick Cottrell will explore how writers respond to a world in transition—and how reading can help us navigate uncertainty, grief, and change. Unferth will read from her new novel, Earth 7 (Graywolf 2026), which explores climate disaster, grief, and humanity’s relationship with the planet. She will then join Cottrell, author of Afternoon Hours of a Hermit (HarperCollins 2026), for a conversation about adaptation, transition, and change—central subjects in both of their work. Together, Unferth and Cottrell will consider what continues to make the novel “novel” and how writers find new ways to see and reflect on ourselves and the world around us. Their conversation will explore what reading and writing can offer when the world seems lost—and how literature might help us imagine what comes next. Free and open to the public -- but please register at the link provided. Contact Meghan Maloney-Vinz at mvinz01@hamline.edu with questions about this event or the Vane Creative Artist Series.

title: Erik Brandt & the Folksingers
description:
Erik Brandt has been the ringleader of the award-winning eclectic Twin Cities-based Urban Hillbilly Quartet since 1995. By night, he plays music. By day, he teaches high school English in St. Paul, MN. He’s played in venues all over the USA, Canada, Australia, and on various street corners throughout Europe. He’s also taught Shakespeare, grammar, haikus and standardized test prep.

On stage, Erik performs mainly original material drawn from the Americana vein. Most of his original tunes can be found on the nine albums he’s recorded with the UHQ and his four solo albums, including his latest, Folksinger. When choosing covers, he pulls liberally from the catalogs of Bob Dylan, The Flatlanders, Johnny Cash, and other Americana heroes. As a multi-instrumentalist, Erik switches between acoustic guitar, piano and accordion during performances.

His music has been influenced by and compared to: Americana powerhouses The Jayhawks, Gillian Welch, and Uncle Tupelo; Georgia’s Vigilantes of Love; Britain’s The Waterboys; Australia’s Paul Kelly; Canada’s Bruce Cockburn; and folk/jazz pioneers David Grisman, Paris Combo and Tin Hat Trio.

He’s the DJ and host of “Good Acoustics” on 88.5 KBEM-FM and also accordionist for the Roe Family Singers and Mega Yacht Jazz Combo.

Though Erik mostly performs solo, he is often joined by guests from UHQ and other bands on stage. The combination of his different instruments, songwriting talent and musical guests makes his live performances dynamic and unique.
